item.text: {"decisions":[{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0001","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0001 contains only CIDOB website navigation elements, header/footer boilerplate, and basic biographical metadata (name, role, dates, party affiliation, editor credit). No substantive economic governance content is present.","exclusion_reason":"Pure website navigation and metadata content; no economic governance content whatsoever."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0002","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0002 covers López Obrador's rise through the 1990s PRD, the video scandal involving his subordinates, and his DF government management. The videoescándalo section touches on corruption allegations against close allies, but the unit is structured as political biography focusing on electoral trajectory, party leadership, and the 2004-2005 desafuero crisis. No substantive discussion of economic governance mechanisms, fiscal policy implementation, institutional economic reforms, or budget execution outcomes.","exclusion_reason":"Political biography covering video scandal, desafuero crisis, and party leadership; no substantive economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0003","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0003 covers the contested 2006 presidential election result (0.56% margin lost to Calderón), López Obrador's rejection of the outcome, his claim of fraud, and his parallel government declaration. This is electoral contest narrative and opposition strategy, not economic governance discussion.","exclusion_reason":"Electoral contest narrative and opposition strategy; no economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0004","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0004 covers the 2012 electoral defeat to Peña Nieto, the electoral court challenge, and the September 2012 split from PRD to found MORENA. Opposition strategy and party founding history. The critique of Peña Nieto's policies mentions economic themes (corruption, incompetence, basic goods prices) but only as opposition framing, not substantive governance analysis.","exclusion_reason":"Opposition strategy and party founding narrative; no substantive economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0005","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.6","5B.8","5B.9"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0006"],"explanation":"Unit-0005 presents the 2018 campaign program 'Proyecto 2018' of the Juntos Haremos Historia coalition. It contains substantive economic governance proposals: (1) 'austeridad republicana' to reorient public resources from current spending to investment without raising taxes; (2) social causes including poverty combat and human development for vulnerable populations; (3) reduction of fuel imports and domestic price reduction via increased domestic gasoline output; (4) energy and food self-sufficiency with guaranteed prices for local agricultural producers; (5) corruption eradication by example from Los Pinos; (6) immigration policy linked to economic cooperation with the US. These directly address 5B.1 (prosperity agenda vs rents/loyalty), 5B.3 (fiscal rules and macroeconomic discipline), 5B.6 (investment vs patronage), 5B.8 (distribution to vulnerable populations), and 5B.9 (fuel price shock management).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0006","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.4","5B.10"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0005","unit-0007"],"explanation":"Unit-0006 characterizes the 2018-2024 government platform as 'pragmatic social democracy' that assumes orthodox free market principles, macroeconomic stability, budgetary discipline, and peso flotation, combined with rejection of privatization and foreign domination of strategic sectors, and prioritization of national production. It states that the platform combines reassuring signals to entrepreneurs with promises of ending corruption and privileges of former presidents. These statements directly address 5B.1 (prosperity agenda), 5B.3 (credible fiscal/monetary rules protecting macroeconomic stability), 5B.4 (competition and investment framework), and 5B.10 (economic trajectory vs inherited framework).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0007","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0007 covers the post-election period from late 2018 including USMCA trade negotiations, Central American migrant caravans at the US-Mexico border, and Trump's threat to close the border. These are foreign trade and migration policy topics, not economic governance evaluation under the 5B framework.","exclusion_reason":"Migration and border policy context; no substantive economic governance content for 5B questions."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0008","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0008 begins the detailed political biography from birth (1953) through early life, family tragedy, move to Mexico City, university enrollment, and early PRI activism. Pure biographical narrative with no economic governance content.","exclusion_reason":"Political biography from birth through early career; no economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0009","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0009 covers university enrollment (UNAM Faculty of Political Science), early party activism with PRI, introduction to Leandro Rovirosa Wade governor of Tabasco, and INI delegation work in La Chontalpa with indigenous communities. Pure biographical narrative; INI work mentions social programs but without economic governance evaluation.","exclusion_reason":"Early political career within PRI; no substantive economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0010","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0010 covers COPLAMAR delegation (1978), university teaching, marriage and family formation, and 1982 campaign work for Enrique González Pedrero's gubernatorial campaign. Pure biographical narrative of party and government work in Tabasco.","exclusion_reason":"Early party and government work biography; no economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0011","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0011 covers PRI committee leadership in Tabasco, internal party disputes leading to 1983 dismissal, return to Mexico City with INCO position, university graduation thesis on Mexican state formation, and 1987 Democratic Current formation within PRI. Pure party political biography, including internal PRI faction disputes.","exclusion_reason":"Internal party political biography; no substantive economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0012","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0012 covers the 1988 elections (both presidential and gubernatorial), the alleged 'computer system collapse,' Salinas victory, and López Obrador's gubernatorial defeat. Electoral history narrative and fraud allegation recounting.","exclusion_reason":"1988 electoral history and fraud allegations; no economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0013","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0013 covers PRD founding (May 1989), the 1991-1992 democracy march from Tabasco to Mexico City, and post-march electoral negotiation outcomes. Party founding narrative and street protest/mobilization history.","exclusion_reason":"PRD founding and street mobilization history; no economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0014","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0014 covers the 1994 gubernatorial election in Tabasco (lost to Roberto Madrazo with 38.7%), fraud allegations, and subsequent mobilization campaign including the 1995 'caravana por la democracia' and National Democratic Alliance formation. Electoral contest narrative and opposition mobilization.","exclusion_reason":"Electoral contest and opposition mobilization in Tabasco; no economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0015","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0015 covers PRD party presidency election (July 1996, 73.9% of votes), book publication on corruption and Tabasco democracy struggle, and context of PRD electoral failures. Party leadership narrative.","exclusion_reason":"PRD party presidency election and electoral context; no economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0016","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0016 covers PRD electoral successes in 1997 (DF government, legislative assembly, federal congress), 1998-1999 state gubernatorial wins, and 1999 party presidency handover to Pablo Gómez. Party electoral success narrative.","exclusion_reason":"PRD electoral victories 1997-1999; no economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0017","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0017 covers Cárdenas' resignation from DF government (September 1999) to prepare for presidential run, López Obrador's primary campaign for DF mayor candidacy (November 1999, 75.5%), and his FOBAPROA investigation book. Political biography and opposition research into bank rescue fund.","exclusion_reason":"DF primary campaign and FOBAPROA opposition research; political biography without substantive economic governance evaluation."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0018","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0018 covers the July 2000 federal elections (Fox victory, Cárdenas third place, López Obrador's DF mayoral win with 34.5%), electoral context of the broader PAN victory. Electoral history narrative.","exclusion_reason":"2000 federal electoral history; no economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0019","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0019 covers López Obrador's DF government inauguration (December 2000), the death of his father, and an overview of his 2000-2005 DF governance period as a decisive phase in his national trajectory. General character assessment and biographical framing for the DF government period.","exclusion_reason":"DF government inauguration and general character overview; no substantive economic governance evaluation."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0020","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0020 covers López Obrador's personal attributes (charisma, tenacity, nickname 'Peje'), public communication style (early morning press conferences 'mananeras'), and the deeply ambivalent public assessment of his governance. General character and communication style assessment, not economic governance analysis.","exclusion_reason":"Personal character and communication style assessment; no substantive economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0021","included":true,"relevant_question_ids":["5B.6","5B.8"],"relevance_strength":"material","adjacent_chunk_ids":["unit-0020","unit-0022"],"explanation":"Unit-0021 presents concrete outcomes of López Obrador's DF government (2000-2005): (1) vigorous public works campaign for urban infrastructure improvement and expansion; (2) social protection programs, most notably the Pensión Universal Alimenticia para Adultos Mayores (universal food pension for seniors); (3) refusal to implement the federal Seguro Popular health insurance on the grounds that DF residents already received free municipal social coverage. These represent actual executed budget outcomes and social program design, directly relevant to 5B.6 (budget quality and infrastructure/social investment vs patronage) and 5B.8 (distribution across social groups including seniors).","exclusion_reason":null},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0022","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0022 covers the March 2004 video scandal (videoescándalo), Televisa broadcast of clandestine recordings showing PRD officials including René Bejarano engaged in money-for-favors negotiations with businessman Carlos Ahumada. Corruption events narrative and scandal management.","exclusion_reason":"Corruption scandal narrative; political biography without substantive economic governance evaluation."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0023","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0023 continues the video scandal aftermath, PRD internal damage, charges against involved officials, Rosario Robles forced to leave the party, and López Obrador's response attributing the scandal to a political conspiracy by Salinas, Fernández de Cevallos, and the Fox government. Political biography and opposition response to corruption allegations.","exclusion_reason":"Video scandal aftermath and political attribution; no substantive economic governance evaluation."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0024","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0024 covers the May 2004 desafuero request by the PGR for López Obrador's arrest and prosecution related to a minor land expropriation case in Cuajimalpa from 2000. Political-juridical battle narrative.","exclusion_reason":"Desafuero political-juridical process; no economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0025","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0025 covers the August 2004 demonstration of 200,000 PRD supporters, López Obrador's book on national project, and the November 2004 removal of Marcelo Ebrard as security secretary by President Fox following the Tláhuac lynching incident. Political mobilization and personnel dispute narrative.","exclusion_reason":"Political mobilization and federal-state personnel dispute; no economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0026","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0026 covers the April 2005 Chamber of Deputies vote approving desafuero (360-127), López Obrador's civil resistance mobilization, and the constitutional conflict between the federal government and DF Assembly over his removal from office. Political mobilization and constitutional conflict narrative.","exclusion_reason":"Desafuero vote and constitutional conflict; no economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0027","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0027 covers the May 2005 PGR case collapse (prosecution unable to get a judge to initiate proceedings), Fox's acceptance of López Obrador's candidacy rights, and the May 2005 charges withdrawal and archive by new prosecutor Daniel Cabeza de Vaca. Political-juridical resolution narrative.","exclusion_reason":"Desafuero legal resolution; no economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0028","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0028 covers López Obrador's July 2005 departure from DF government to focus on PRD primary, Alejandro Encinas as interim replacement, his unchallenged designation as PRD presidential candidate (September), and his December 2005 oath as coalition candidate 'Por el Bien de Todos.' Candidacy designation narrative.","exclusion_reason":"Presidential candidacy designation; no economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0029","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0029 covers the 2006 campaign dynamics: Calderón's 'FeCal' nickname, López Obrador's radicalism creating apprehension among middle classes, the two candidates being practically tied in June polls, and López Obrador's allegations against Calderón regarding nepotism and abuse of power when director of BANOBRAS and Energy secretary. Electoral campaign narrative.","exclusion_reason":"2006 electoral campaign dynamics; no substantive economic governance evaluation."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0030","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0030 covers the 2006 campaign program of the Por el Bien de Todos coalition: ending the privilege/corruption/sack system, austerity in government (halving presidential salary), fraud and tax evasion fighting, FOBAPROA investigation by a Truth Commission, and social programs extending public services to degraded areas. Electoral program overview without implementation evidence.","exclusion_reason":"2006 electoral campaign program; political promises without implementation evidence. For 5B assessment, implementation lag means campaign programs from before taking office are excluded unless tied to concrete governance mechanisms."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0031","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0031 continues the 2006 Por el Bien de Todos electoral program: social development programs, agricultural/tourism/construction sectors, energy sector reform (no privatization of Pemex), minimum wage defense, and foreign policy positions (NAFTA agricultural chapter, migration not resolved with walls or militarization). Electoral program without implementation evidence.","exclusion_reason":"2006 electoral program continuation; political promises without implementation evidence."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0032","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0032 covers López Obrador's distancing from Chávez/Venezuela, the June 2006 polling data showing him tied or trailing Calderón (33-36% range for both), and context of high electoral polarization. Electoral positioning and polling context.","exclusion_reason":"Electoral positioning and polling context; no substantive economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0033","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0033 covers the July 2006 election night: initial PREP showing Calderón ahead by 400,000 votes (0.64% margin), EU observer mission confirmation of cleanliness, and the second mutual proclamation of victory by both candidates. Electoral night narrative.","exclusion_reason":"2006 election night narrative; no economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0034","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0034 covers the TEPJF recount decision (August 5, partial recount of 9% of polling stations), international electoral mission validation, PRD's good legislative results contrasting with presidential challenge, and López Obrador's escalation of protests. Post-electoral dispute and mobilization narrative.","exclusion_reason":"Post-2006 electoral dispute and protest mobilization; no economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0035","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0035 covers the TEPJF partial recount result (237,000 votes annulled, Calderón's margin unchanged at 0.56%), López Obrador's fury and 'usurper' characterization of Calderón, congressional protest blocking Fox's annual address, and intensification of resistance. Post-electoral conflict escalation narrative.","exclusion_reason":"Post-electoral conflict escalation; no economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0036","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0036 covers the September 2006 congressional protest, National Democratic Convention (CND) convocation, 'legitimate government' formation with 12 secretaries, and the November 20 million-strong Zócalo rally where López Obrador was proclaimed 'legitimate president.' Opposition mobilization and parallel government formation narrative.","exclusion_reason":"Opposition parallel government formation; no economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0037","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0037 covers López Obrador's second marriage (October 2007) and the November 20, 2006 'inauguration' ceremony of the parallel government with the tricolor presidential sash, with senator Rosario Ybarra placing the sash. Parallel government inauguration ceremony narrative.","exclusion_reason":"Personal life event and parallel government ceremony; no economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0038","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0038 covers the December 1, 2006 inauguration chaos in Congress, Calderón's brief ceremony and relocation to the National Auditorium, and López Obrador's parallel Zócalo rally denouncing the 'usurper.' Opposition inauguration day narrative.","exclusion_reason":"Opposition inauguration day narrative; no economic governance content."},{"schema_version":"chunk_routing_decision_v1","source_id":"BOOK-013","source_sha256":"8278f6eaaceb659d4fd8928072c46884f894d0c9826a1752e6ddbef53739da80","chunk_id":"unit-0039","included":false,"relevant_question_ids":[],"relevance_strength":"none","adjacent_chunk_ids":[],"explanation":"Unit-0039 covers 2007-2008 opposition activities: sustained mass rallies, Mandoki's documentary 'Fraud: Mexico 2006,' and international non-recognition of the parallel government.
